title: Ashgrove Fixed Indexed Annuities — Number of Contracts per Owner and Covered Persons
content:
**New business guideline — holdings of Fixed Indexed Annuities**

**Rule.** An owner may hold any number of Ashgrove Fixed Indexed Annuities contracts; the count is not capped. No annuitant may be the covered person under more than one IncomeShield lifetime withdrawal benefit. Total premium on one annuitant is governed by the per-annuitant aggregate premium limit.

### The rule in three parts

| Question the rule answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of Fixed Indexed Annuities contracts per owner? | No — there is no cap on the count. |
| May one annuitant be the covered person under two IncomeShield lifetime withdrawal benefits? | No — one IncomeShield lifetime withdrawal benefit per covered person at most. |
| What limits the total premium placed on one annuitant? | The per-annuitant aggregate premium limit. |

### Points of judgement (hypothetical holdings)

- *An owner already holds an Ashgrove IndexEdge 5 and an Ashgrove IndexEdge 7 and applies for an Ashgrove IndexEdge 10.* The number of contracts held places no bar on the new contract.
- *An annuitant is already the covered person under the lifetime withdrawal benefit of an Ashgrove IncomeShield 7.* The same annuitant may not also be the covered person under the lifetime withdrawal benefit of a second IncomeShield contract, whether an IncomeShield 7 or an IncomeShield 10.
- *An annuitant is the covered person under one Ashgrove IncomeShield 10 and is also the annuitant on an Ashgrove IndexEdge 10.* The IndexEdge 10 carries no lifetime withdrawal benefit, so it creates no second covered-person position under an IncomeShield benefit.

The limit on covered persons attaches to the annuitant, not to the owner: two different annuitants on contracts of one owner are two different covered persons.
